title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
gist: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital extended $150M conditional loans each to Stoke Space and Rocket Lab, signalling defense concern over a launch supply crunch as SpaceX winds down Falcon 9 commercial service after 2028 to prioritize Starship. Rocket Lab is raising Neutron pricing from $55M to $70M on a 117-launch backlog, evidence of pricing power in a constrained launch market.

insights.claim: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) committed a $150 million conditional loan to Stoke Space on October 26, 2026 and a second $150 million conditional loan to Rocket Lab two weeks later, the first significant OSC support for launch companies.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Government-backed cheap debt de-risks capex for SpaceX challengers; watch RKLB balance sheet and private Stoke valuations.

insights.claim: The OSC, created in 2022 to fund 'vital' national security technologies, has been on a loan spree committing hundreds of millions of dollars to batteries, drones, semiconductors, and $150 million to satellite tracker LeoLabs for radar deployment.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: OSC loans are an emerging financing channel for defense-tech companies across batteries, drones, chips and space.

insights.claim: Stoke Space's OSC loan funds a second launch pad at Cape Canaveral for its Nova Block 2 rocket, an upgrade of the fully reusable Nova Pathfinder due to debut in 2027.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Infrastructure funding shortens Stoke's path to national security launch eligibility.

insights.claim: Rocket Lab's OSC loan targets Neutron flight rate: faster vehicle delivery, more maritime recovery vessels, increased composite structure and engine production, and infrastructure to cut turnaround between launches.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Funds go to cadence rather than development, implying the Pentagon expects Neutron to fly and wants volume.

insights.claim: SpaceX has stopped taking commercial Falcon 9 orders for launches after 2028 as it shifts to Starship; Space Force can order Falcon 9/Heavy through 2029 with launches extending through 2033.

insights.so_what: A dated end to the dominant workhorse rocket creates a capacity gap that competitors can price into.

insights.claim: The Pentagon's sudden financing of SpaceX competitors suggests defense officials view the retirement of Falcon 9 as a potential national security risk.

insights.so_what: Expect more policy support for alternative launch providers under the assured-access-to-space doctrine.

insights.claim: Rocket Lab raised Neutron's per-launch price from $55 million to $70 million, citing a surge in bookings for the unflown rocket, and reports a 117-launch backlog across Neutron and Electron.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A ~27% price hike pre-first-flight signals real pricing power in a supply-constrained launch market.

insights.claim: Rocket Lab's leadership frames launch as a supply-constrained market where capital helps unlock capacity, describing the Pentagon loan as on 'very attractive terms'.

insights.so_what: Management sees capacity, not demand, as the binding constraint — margin upside if Neutron executes.
